parts.problem_md:
Bioaccumulation and biomagnification are two impacts of plastic pollution on marine ecosystems.

Describe other impacts of plastic pollution on marine ecosystems.
parts.solution_md:
Animals such as turtles and seabirds become entangled in plastic  **[1 mark]**, so they cannot swim or feed properly  **[1 mark]**. Animals mistake floating plastic for food  **[1 mark]**, which blocks their digestive system and can cause starvation  **[1 mark]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This answer is assessed using a point-marked approach.
> 
> - One mark for each valid point
> - Maximum 4 marks
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Other information that could be used includes:
> 
> - Floating plastic and litter on beaches cause visual pollution
> - People may stop using polluted beaches and coastal waters
> - Any other suitable response
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> - Repeating bioaccumulation or biomagnification, which the question has already given
> - Writing 'it causes pollution' without saying what the plastic does

> **[exam-tip]**
> - For a four-mark 'describe', give an impact and then say what it does to the animal. Each impact plus its effect can earn two marks.

parts.problem_md:
Biodegradable bioplastics break down over time.

Suggest two abiotic factors that affect the rate of break down of biodegradable bioplastics.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Any **two** from:
> 
> - Temperature
> - Water (moisture)
> - Soil pH
> - Oxygen
> - Salinity
> - Light
> 
> **[2 marks]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Abiotic means non-living. Living factors such as the number of bacteria are biotic, so they do not score here.

parts.problem_md:
Biodegradable bioplastics break down over time.

Name two products formed when biodegradable bioplastics break down.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> Unnamed 'gases' are not credited.
> 
> Any **two** from:
> 
> - Water
> - Biomass
> - Carbon dioxide
> - Methane
> 
> **[2 marks]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Name the gas. 'Gases' on its own does not score, but 'carbon dioxide' or 'methane' does.

parts.problem_md:
Biodegradable bioplastics break down over time.

Name one group of organisms that break down biodegradable bioplastics.

Figure 5.1 shows the global production of non-biodegradable bioplastics and biodegradable bioplastics in 2021 and 2023.

![Stacked bar chart of global production of non-biodegradable and biodegradable bioplastics: 2021 totals 1,800 thousand tonnes and 2023 totals 2,400. The 2025 bar is blank for plotting. y-axis 0–5,000 thousand tonnes.](assets/001-stacked-bar-chart-of-global-production-of-non-bi.png)

*Figure 5.1*

Determine the mass of non-biodegradable bioplastics produced in 2023.

Give the unit.
parts.solution_md:
Top of the 2023 bar = 2400 thousand tonnes and top of the biodegradable section = 1300 thousand tonnes  **[1 mark]**

2400 - 1300 = **1100**  **[1 mark]**

Unit: **thousand tonnes**  **[1 mark]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - **One mark** for reading both values from the graph
> - **One mark** for the subtraction
> - **One mark** for a unit that matches your value: 1100 thousand tonnes or 1 100 000 tonnes

> **[exam-tip]**
> - Read the non-biodegradable section as the difference between two readings, not as the top of the bar.

parts.problem_md:
Figure 5.1 shows the global production of non-biodegradable bioplastics and biodegradable bioplastics in 2021 and 2023.

![Stacked bar chart of global production of non-biodegradable and biodegradable bioplastics: 2021 totals 1,800 thousand tonnes and 2023 totals 2,400. The 2025 bar is blank for plotting. y-axis 0–5,000 thousand tonnes.](assets/001-stacked-bar-chart-of-global-production-of-non-bi.png)

*Figure 5.1*

Table 5.1 shows the predicted global production of non-biodegradable bioplastics and biodegradable bioplastics in 2025.

**Table 5.1**

| year | global production of non-biodegradable bioplastics / thousand tonnes | global production of biodegradable bioplastics / thousand tonnes |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 | 2500 | 2400 |

Plot the data for 2025 on the grid in Figure 5.1.
parts.solution_md:
Draw a stacked bar for 2025. The biodegradable section goes from 0 to 2400 thousand tonnes, and the non-biodegradable section sits on top of it, from 2400 to 4900 thousand tonnes  **[1 mark]**.

Shade each section to match the key and draw the bar the same width as the 2021 and 2023 bars  **[1 mark]**.

> **[exam-tip]**
> - This is a stacked bar chart, so the top of the bar shows the total: 2400 + 2500 = 4900. Plotting the non-biodegradable section from 0 to 2500 is a common mistake.
